html:
The Ottoman constitution of 1876, the Kanun-i Esasi or "Basic Law", was the first written constitution of the Ottoman Empire. It set up an elected parliament beside the sultan.

It crowned the Tanzimat reforms. Reformers led by Midhat Pasha pushed it through when the empire faced war with Russia and pressure from Europe over its Christian subjects. The new sultan, Abdul Hamid II, agreed to it.

The parliament met in 1877, with Muslim, Christian and Jewish deputies. Abdul Hamid used his power under the constitution to exile Midhat, and in 1878, during the war with Russia, he suspended parliament. He ruled alone for thirty years.

The Young Turk Revolution of 1908 forced him to restore the constitution, opening the Second Constitutional Era, which lasted until the empire ended in 1922. It inspired constitutional movements nearby, such as the Persian Constitutional Revolution.
sum: The Ottoman constitution of 1876, the Kanun-i Esasi or "Basic Law", was the first written constitution of the Ottoman Empire. It set up an elected parliament beside the sultan.
